hints: Look at the before diagram where $u_X$ points right and $u_Y$ points left, and the after diagram where $v_X$ points left and $v_Y$ points right.
Recall that perfectly elastic means the relative speed at which the two balls come together equals the relative speed at which they move apart.
Add the two speeds when motion is head-on toward each other, and add the two speeds again when motion is apart in opposite directions.
walkthrough: Identify the speeds as magnitudes: before, X moves right with $u_X$ and Y moves left with $u_Y$ toward each other; after, X moves left with $v_X$ and Y moves right with $v_Y$ away from each other.
State the governing rule for a perfectly elastic collision along one line: speed of approach = speed of separation.
Calculate speed of approach before collision. Because they move toward each other, the closing rate is the sum $u_X + u_Y$.
Calculate speed of separation after collision. Because they move apart in opposite directions, the opening rate is the sum $v_X + v_Y$.
Equate approach and separation to get $u_X + u_Y = v_X + v_Y$. This is option A.

options.A: Relative speed of approach $u_X + u_Y$ equals relative speed of separation $v_X + v_Y$ for a perfectly elastic collision.
options.B: Subtracting $v_Y$ would give the separation as a difference, but the balls separate in opposite directions so their speeds add.
options.C: Subtracting $u_Y$ would give the approach as a difference, but the balls approach head-on so their speeds add.
options.D: Using differences on both sides treats both motions as if in the same direction, which contradicts the before and after diagrams.
